subject: IaC review: namespace abstraction + eBPF L4 load balancer for on-prem
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah@vectorcloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: IaC review: namespace abstraction + eBPF L4 load balancer for on-prem

Team — kicking off a short review thread for the on-prem IaC changes that touch three areas: namespace abstraction in TF, Helm/values for the per-tenant k8s surface, and the proposed eBPF-based L4 load balancer (we're testing Cilium's maglev-style L4).

High level asks:
- Can infra/Terraform owners sign off on the namespace mapping approach (tenant -> VPC/VRF -> k8s namespace)?
- Are there any red flags for the Helm values changes which add a new per-namespace overlay (securityContext, hostPort restrictions)?
- Networking: eBPF L4 LB will require SR-IOV passthrough on some hosts and updated iptables/iptables-compat fallbacks. Ops, can you validate the compatibility matrix?

I've attached a small patch (iac-diff.patch) showing the TF module surface changes, and a sample helm-values-namespace.yaml showing the new overlays. Link to PR and Confluence page below.

Immediate next step: quick thumbs-up or explicit blocker by EOD PST so we can include in next week's release. If you need a call, propose times and I'll set up.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: iac-diff.patch (text), helm-values-namespace.yaml (yaml)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah@vectorcloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IaC review: namespace abstraction + eBPF L4 load balancer for on-prem

Thanks Hannah — quick notes after scanning the patch and values file: 

1) Namespace abstraction in TF modules- I like the explicit mapping table (tenant_id -> vrf_id -> k8s_namespace). Suggestion: add a validate block to the module variables that asserts namespace name length and allowed characters to avoid downstream Helm failures. Also we should emit a state tag describing "networking-profile" per namespace so we can query via Terraform state for audits.

2) Helm overlays- The securityContext changes are fine but we should not enable hostPort support by default. If you need hostPort for the eBPF datapath on a subset of nodes, make it opt-in by nodeSelector label and document the operational tradeoffs.

3) eBPF L4 LB- Ops compatibility concerns below (I'll loop in network team if needed):
   - SR-IOV: requires node config and VF allocation — add an Ansible role that preps nodes (drivers, sriov config) and gate it behind a boolean flag in TF.
   - Fallback: ensure we automatically flip to kube-proxy/ipvs mode when Cilium datapath fails during upgrade; add a rollout probe that validates L4 service health before shifting traffic.

I'll add inline comments on the PR (link). My vote: proceed with the changes if we add the variable validation, the Ansible preparation role, and a canary probe for L4 failover.

Irene
Irene Choi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: ansible-role-networking.tar.gz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah@vectorcloud.com>, ops@edgeworks.io
Date: 2026-08-24T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IaC review: namespace abstraction + eBPF L4 load balancer for on-prem

Looping in a couple of operational notes from my side: 

- Terraform: we should avoid embedding cloud-specific network constructs in the core namespace module. Instead, add a network_profile input that accepts a map of provider-specific metadata. That keeps the module portable across on-prem/edge/cloud.

- CI gating: propose adding a GitLab pipeline job (nf-integration) that validates the TF plan + Helm dry-run against a small, ephemeral k8s cluster (kind with CNI simulation). If the change touches 'network_profile' or 'sriov' flags, require a manual approval stage.

- Rollouts: add a step in the deployment job that stages eBPF config to a single rack (nodeLabel: eBPF-canary) then runs the L4 health probes and service acceptance tests before wider rollout. Make this an explicit rollout in the runbook (I can draft this).

From a Terraform ownership perspective, happy to sign off once the validate block and network_profile separation are in place.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra Engineer, Private Stack
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lee <sarah@vectorcloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ops@edgeworks.io
Date: 2026-08-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: IaC review: namespace abstraction + eBPF L4 load balancer for on-prem

Appreciate the context and the detailed asks. From VectorCloud's side: we've validated Cilium's eBPF L4 in our lab against similar SR-IOV and iptables fallback scenarios. Key notes: 

- Driver compatibility: Dell R7525 and HPE ProLiant gen10+ are in our compatibility matrix for the SR-IOV flows; sending a short compatibility CSV as a follow-up.
- Security/audit: the namespace "networking-profile" tag suggestion is good; in our SOC2 audits we also require an immutable record of any time hostPort or macvlan is enabled — we can emit those events to your audit topic.
- Onboarding: we'll provide an operator playbook for the Ansible role and a demo runbook for the eBPF canary.

We don't see blockers from VectorCloud. Happy to demo the eBPF canary next week.

Regards,
Sarah Lee
Solutions Architect
VectorCloud
